text:
li-huang: Heads up — I ran a quick sweep of per-GPU batch admission failures after the continuous-batching changes. TL;DR: A10/T4 are fine with current caps, L4 and H100 need a safety margin, A100 showing weird kernel fallbacks.

samir: Can you paste the failure kinds? Is this admission (max tokens) rejects or runtime OOMs?

li-huang: Mostly admission rejects (queue decides request won't fit into next batch). No OOMs. But we see elevated tail latency because many requests get requeued and hit canary fallback.

ana: @li-huang do you have sequence length distribution? Might be heavier tails than before.

li-huang: Yes, posted hist: p50=32, p90=128, p99=480. We apply per-card token ceiling (tokens_per_batch) and a per-request token cap. With current ceilings: A10=4096, T4=3072, L4=3072, A100=8192, H100=12288.

jess: Those look like raw device ceilings. We were planning a headroom factor of 0.9 for continuous batching to allow kernel alignment and KV frag. Are you using that?

li-huang: Not uniformly. Some pools use 0.95, some 1.0. When set to 1.0 we see more kernel selector mismatches (falls back to slower kernel path for long sequences) and more KV-fragmentation rejections.

samir: I profiled an L4 run with headroom=1.0 vs 0.88. With 1.0 the scheduler attempted large packings that changed kernel sel from fused-attn -> fallback-attn for ~8% of batches. Latency tail +120ms. With 0.88 kernel sel stabilized and tail improved ~80ms.

perf-bot: perf summary (L4): headroom=1.0 -> p99 latency 640ms; headroom=0.88 -> p99 latency 560ms; throughput delta ~ -3% for 0.88.

ana: So lower headroom improved latency but cost slightly throughput. That’s expected — we trade packing density for kernel fit and fewer requeues.

li-huang: For H100 the problem is different. It accepts huge token batches but KV cache fragmentation creates many small KV allocations leading to poorer memory locality. Some kernels expect contiguous KV buffers and perform worse. We saw a kernel switch to a new path that is ~15% slower for dense KV fragmentation cases.

samir: For A100 we saw unpredictable kernel selector behavior: when batch tokens ~6500 it tries a float16 fast kernel that has stricter alignment, but a single request with odd seq_len triggers scalar path for the batch. That scalar path latency spike cascades.

jess: Thanks — this motivates per-GPU safety margins tuned to kernel selection sensitivity, not just raw device memory. Proposal: store two ceilings per GPU type: admitted_tokens_soft and admitted_tokens_hard. Soft uses headroom factor for kernel-friendly packing; hard is absolute max to avoid OOMs. Scheduler should prefer soft and only use hard when low queue pressure and confidence in kernel fit.

li-huang: Agreed. Also propose per-pool kernel-confidence metric (0..1) from perf-bot that measures fraction of batches that used fast kernel. Use that to nudge headroom dynamically.

samir: I sketched a config experiment:
```
# example pool config
gpu_type: L4
admitted_tokens_soft: 0.88 * device_ceiling
admitted_tokens_hard: 0.98 * device_ceiling
kernel_confidence_threshold: 0.92
adjust_step: 0.02
```
Scheduler pseudocode: prefer soft; if kernel_confidence > threshold and queue_len < Q_LOW then increase soft by adjust_step (cap at hard); if kernel_confidence < threshold decrease soft by adjust_step.

perf-bot: Quick sim results (based on 24h trace): L4 baseline soft=0.95 -> p99 620ms; dynamic soft -> p99 540ms; throughput -1.5%. H100 baseline -> p99 410ms; dynamic -> p99 380ms; throughput -0.8%. A100 dynamic avoided scalar path 92% of the time vs 84% baseline.

ana: Nice. What about request requeue churn? That was causing tail with lots of retries.

li-huang: Requeue rate reduced from 3.4% -> 1.1% on L4 in sim. Most requeues were due to admission rejection after provisional packing (when kernel mismatch detected at selection time). We should surface a metrics tag: admission_reason=[kv_frag|kernel_mismatch|mem_ceiling].

jess: Good idea. Ops wants alerting on requeue rate >2% per pool and kernel_confidence drop below 0.85.

ops-bot: Alert rule noted: requeue_rate > 0.02 OR kernel_confidence < 0.85 -> notify #eng-runtime on-call.

samir: One more caveat: quantized kernels (int8/q4) have different alignment and KV layout expectations. When we switch models to q4 we must run a short kernel-fit job to calibrate admitted_tokens_soft for that model+gpu combo. Otherwise kernel_confidence will tank.

li-huang: Plan for experiments this week: 1) Run dynamic-soft policy on staging pools L4/A100/H100 for 48h with tracing enabled. 2) Add admission_reason tags to Scheduler. 3) Add per-model quick-fit step post-quantization. 4) Tune default soft factors: A10:0.93, T4:0.9, L4:0.88, A100:0.92, H100:0.9 (starting values).

jess: Sounds good. Can you open a runbook PR with the steps and the alert thresholds? Keep the PR small.

li-huang: Will do. I'll also drop a short table of the default soft factors and sim numbers into the PR.

samir: If staging looks good we'll roll to canary for 6h on low-traffic pools then gradual ramp. Watch kernel_confidence and requeue_reason.

li-huang: Thanks all. Posting raw sim outputs and plots next message.

perf-bot: uploaded perf artifacts: /artifacts/2410000000/device-safety-sim.tar.gz

jess: Great — enough to open the PR. :thumbsup:
